newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Yukong sees petroleum exports tripling.
newsitem.headline: Yukong sees petroleum exports tripling.

text.p: Yukong Ltd, South Korea's largest oil refiner, plans to expand its oil products exports to 130,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 30,000-45,000 bpd with full operation of its new 200,000 bpd crude distillation unit (CDU), a company spokesman said on Friday.

"We plan to sell abroad around 50 percent of the output from the new unit," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone in Seoul. Yukong currently has an overall crude processing capability of 610,000 bpd, he said.
Yukong's new 451 billion-won CDU is expected to start full commercial production by September 30. A new 60,000-bpd middle distillates desulphuriser is following a similar schedule, he said.
The refiner hopes to sell 1.5 million barrels of gas oil overseas on a monthly basis against 1.0-1.2 million currently, a company source said.
"Most of the increased output is expected to be shipped to China," he said.
Traders said China also will be the main target for Korean exports because its geographical proximity means delivered prices will be more attractive for Chinese buyers.
The increase in output is also expected to help Yukong reduce the size of its imports, which at present stand at 100,000 bpd, the spokesman said.
He said the new CDU can switch between using high and low sulphur crude oil as a feedstock.
